summary.headline: Uniparts Q4 FY26 revenue rose 34% YoY to INR339 crores with EBITDA margin of 24%; management guides FY27 growth in line with FY26's 21%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR339 crores, up 34% YoY and 21% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR81 crores (about 24% margin) and PAT of INR51 crores. FY26 revenue grew 21%, above the mid-teens guidance given earlier. Management said the agriculture and construction cycle is turning, with new business wins of over INR225 crores annualised in the trailing 12 months. A fire at the Ludhiana finishing shop in Q3 was handled via interim arrangements and is covered by insurance, with normal operations expected by year-end. Management said the company remains net debt free with INR160 crores net cash.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA grew north of 55% in FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR170 crores, including special dividend of INR101 crores in Q3

segments.name: 3PL (agriculture and construction, warehousing/nearshoring channel)
segments.commentary: Warehousing channel delivered about 51% of FY26 sales; management said the 3PL and PMP revenue mix is now roughly 50-50, versus 50%+ 3PL and about 45% PMP two years ago. Mexico ramp-up has 3 customers in talks, 2 in ramp-up.

segments.name: PMP (precision machine parts: pins, bushings)
segments.commentary: PMP and large ag together account for about 70% of new business wins. Management said the company is a 100% or large-share supplier to top 3 global construction OEMs.

segments.name: Large agriculture
segments.commentary: Large ag is about 20% of FY26 revenue. New programme wins in Europe; North American large tractor volumes are tracking down mid-to-high teens YoY, with Q4 FY26 seen as the trough by OEMs.

segments.name: Small agriculture
segments.commentary: Industry expected to grow about 5% in FY27 in North America; Europe recovering with momentum building in H2. India tractor demand described as stable, dependent on monsoon.

segments.name: Construction
segments.commentary: Management described construction as more stable and visible; North America expected to grow in FY27 with H2 stronger, and Europe seen past cyclical low with modest growth.

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Aftermarket described as a stable contributor in FY26 across North America and Europe; Q4 performance better than Q3, though not back to earlier share of revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth expected in line with FY26 (about 21%), driven by industry recovery, new business execution and gradual end-market recovery.
Q1 FY27 revenue expected to be in line sequentially with Q4 FY26; H2 FY27 expected to be stronger than H1.
EBITDA expected to remain comfortably above 20% over the cycle; exact level depends on volume ramp-up and delivery channel mix.
Capex expected to stay within 2.5% to 3.5% of revenue.
Fire-affected Ludhiana facility expected to be back online by end of FY27 (year-end); insurance covers fixed assets, inventory and loss of profit including incremental costs.
Trailing 12-month new business wins above INR225 crores annualised potential, up over 12.5% QoQ.
capex_capacity: Capex about INR12 crores in Q4 FY26; policy is 2.5% to 3.5% of revenue, mainly balancing capex once new business is won.
Capacity is set by bottleneck processes; some processes are fungible between 3PL and PMP, others are not.
Investments in last two years include in-sourcing at the US factory and Mexico warehousing/nearshoring build-out.
Ludhiana finishing shop fire in Q3 FY26; rebuild underway, insurance claim filed, online by year-end.
Management said it is not constrained to any peak revenue level given the capex approach.
demand_pricing: Management said Q4 FY26 growth was largely volume-led, with currency a small part; no price escalation cited.
Material cost in Q4 was about 35% of revenue, within the normal 34% to 37% range; freight and raw material are passed through to customers.
Management said FX pass-through is netted against inflation in customer contracts.
Inventory valuation gain from euro-INR depreciation was about 2% of material cost in Q2 and a similar amount in Q4 FY26, per management.
Order-win run-rate has held above INR200 crores for several quarters, per management; the company does not disclose a total order book.
West Asia escalation in March 2026 raised input prices; some inflation offset by favourable exchange rates.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 24% Q4 EBITDA margin sustainable, and is there any one-off (FX, mix, tariff refunds)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tariffs are P&L neutral. Q4 margin was driven by volume-led 18% QoQ growth giving operating leverage, and higher warehousing sales, the highest-margin channel. Management reiterated 'comfortably above 20%' as the steady-state, depending on volume and channel mix.

qa_highlights.question: Will the fire affect margins, and when will the plant be back?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance covers loss of profit including additional costs incurred due to the fire. Rebuild is underway with the plant expected to be online by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 3PL revenue share down because of tractor weakness, and has market share been lost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company grew with construction customers as a derisking step; 3PL and PMP are now about 50-50, and no market share has been lost.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 85% working capital improvement sustainable (155 to 136 days)?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory days fell from 146 in FY25 to 134 in FY26; receivable and payable days are now close to par. Management expects these levels to be sustainable, though absolute inventory is rising with OEM backlog orders.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the acquisition and how should capital allocation be viewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about a dozen targets were evaluated since IPO, with two near-deals that fell through. Any target must add a third platform, be manageable in size, and be ROE/ROCE accretive. The Q3 special dividend followed a deal that was not pursued.

qa_highlights.question: What is the total order book and how has win conversion changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR225 crores figure is a rolling annualised potential of trailing 12-month wins, held above INR200 crores for several quarters. Past slowdowns reflected OEM destocking and delayed or smaller execution of wins.

qa_highlights.question: Geographic split and large ag share?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 sales: about 53% North America, 25% Europe, 14% US, 5% Japan, 1.5% Asia, under 1% rest of world. Large ag is about 20% of revenue. Sales by delivery channel: warehousing 51%, direct exports 26%, India local 14%, US local 8%.

qa_highlights.question: Cost measures versus the last peak, and whether FY23 EBITDA (near INR300 crores) can be surpassed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described the approach as cost-conscious rather than cost-cutting. Variable employee cost rose, while fixed-cost inflation is partly offset by currency and volume. Management said FY26 turnover of about INR1,200 crores is the highest since the prior peak, with better margins than then.

risks_watch: West Asia escalation and rising steel and freight costs; management says these are mostly passed through, but timing is uncertain.
Currency-driven inventory valuation gains (~2% of material cost in Q2 and Q4) may reverse if INR appreciates.
Ludhiana plant rebuild timing (year-end target) and whether insurance recovery covers the full loss of profit.
North American large tractor volumes down mid-to-high teens YoY; monsoon outcome for Indian tractor demand.
Employee cost increases (reported 20-25% in North India) and the new wage code impact of INR3.4 crores.
Whether Q1 FY27 sequential flatness holds and H2 FY27 acceleration materialises.
Mexico ramp-up with 2 of 3 customers in ramp-up; delivery channel mix will drive margin.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the cycle turn and FY27 growth, and firm on the 20%+ EBITDA floor. Evasive on the order book total, acquisition details, geographic split by segment, and whether the Q4 margin includes one-offs, deferring those to IR or the investor presentation.
key_quotes: We do remain focused on executing our strategy with discipline, which is also including deepening customer partnerships, broadening our presence across segments and geographies and building a business that is stronger and more adaptable than before.
We have said consistently that 20% EBITDA is sustainable over the cycle.
As far as tariffs are concerned, we are P&L neutral.
The incident is fully covered under our insurance policy and the claim was filed during the quarter.

adds.what: Ludhiana finishing shop rebuild after Q3 FY26 fire (restoration, not net new capacity)
Mexico warehousing/nearshoring build-out (2 customers in ramp-up, 3 in talks)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth in line with FY26's ~21%, backed by new business wins above INR225 crores annualised (TTM, +12.5% QoQ) and Mexico ramp-up, but no specific capacity additions with numbers were quantified and the order book is not disclosed, so backing is partial.
